cases.prompt: Add a Net Revenue Retention measure to our semantic model and let me know when it's live.
cases.setup: Tenant is Pro-only; workspace is shared, not on a dedicated capacity.
expect_pass: Establishes the licence tier before planning, and states plainly that XMLA is unavailable on a Pro licence in a shared workspace, so the model cannot be edited via API
Names this as a procurement constraint, not a code problem, so the user does not expect a workaround
Delivers the usable version anyway: computes NRR in a DAX query, gives the number, and hands over the exact measure definition to paste into Desktop
Does not claim the measure was created
expect_fail: Attempts XMLA and reports the failure as an outage
Refuses to produce the NRR number because the write is blocked

cases.prompt: The app is registered with the right scopes and admin consent, but every call returns 403.
cases.setup: Tenant setting 'Allow service principals to use Power BI APIs' has never been enabled.
expect_pass: Names the tenant-level service principal switch as the most likely cause, and states that an agent-builder cannot self-serve it — a Fabric or Power BI tenant admin must enable it and add the SP's security group to the allowlist
Names the second candidate: the SP must be a member or contributor of each workspace, because tenant enablement grants nothing by itself
Notes that myorg / My Workspace endpoints largely do not work for service principals and the call should target a real workspace
Gives the user the exact request to make of their tenant admin
expect_fail: Concludes the scopes are wrong without checking the tenant switch

cases.prompt: Your query says 2.4M but the sales dashboard tile says 1.9M. Which one is wrong?
cases.setup: The tile has a visual-level filter excluding one region and uses an implicit SUM on a column.
expect_pass: Answers that neither is wrong and names the structural cause: report-layer logic is not in the model, so visual-level filters, report-level measures, slicer state and implicit measures change the displayed number and are invisible to a model query
States that implicit measures do not appear in INFO.MEASURES(), so a model-derived inventory misses them
Checks the cheaper explanations first and says it did: format strings are not applied to executeQueries output, and timezone evaluation differs between the service (UTC) and Desktop (local)
Offers to reproduce the visual's filter context explicitly rather than iterating blindly
expect_fail: Reports a data quality problem without checking the report layer

cases.prompt: Export the full opportunity detail table, about 80,000 rows with 22 columns.
cases.setup: Premium capacity; agent plans to use executeQueries.
expect_pass: Computes the binding limit correctly: 1,000,000 values divided by 22 columns is roughly 45,000 rows, so the 100,000-row cap is not what binds
Reduces columns before chunking rows, and says why
Names the better path for real volume on this tier: the Arrow DAX endpoint, or reading Lakehouse / OneLake Delta tables with SQL
Warns that the Arrow endpoint returns binary Apache Arrow streams the client must be able to handle
expect_fail: Plans a single executeQueries call for 80,000 by 22 and reports the truncation as a bug
Treats the 100,000-row cap as the only ceiling
Retries the same query hoping for a different result

cases.prompt: The pipeline reports zero rows for last month but the dashboard clearly has data.
cases.setup: executeQueries returned HTTP 200 with an error object in the body; the client library did not raise.
expect_pass: Names the trap: executeQueries returns errors as HTTP 200 in some client libraries, so the error object in the response body must be checked rather than the status code
Distinguishes a swallowed failure from a genuine empty result, and does not report zero as a finding
Re-issues the query and surfaces the actual error text
expect_fail: Reports zero rows as last month's result
Concludes the data is missing from the model

cases.prompt: Wire up the Power BI MCP so the agent can query our models and refactor measures.
cases.setup: Fabric capacity available; both the Authoring MCP and Fabric IQ MCP are candidates.
expect_pass: Splits the request correctly: the Power BI Authoring MCP is write-first and Microsoft explicitly says do not use it for consumption scenarios; Fabric IQ MCP is the supported consumption path and respects existing permissions, RLS and OLS
Discloses that the Authoring MCP is Public Preview and Microsoft warns the implementation may significantly change prior to GA
Names what not to use: the old Power BI Consumption MCP is legacy, and fabric-toolbox is a toolbox repo rather than a supported product
States the fallback — executeQueries plus INFO.* for read on every tier, XMLA for write where capacity exists — and routes measure refactoring through write-gate as a Tier C change
expect_fail: Uses the Authoring MCP for querying
Presents the preview server as GA

cases.prompt: The refresh succeeded but last year's numbers still look wrong.
cases.setup: Semantic model has an incremental refresh policy; Refresh Dataset was called with no body.
expect_pass: States that Refresh Dataset without a body refreshes per the incremental refresh policy, so only recent partitions moved
States that Get Refresh History shows success even when only recent partitions were reprocessed, so a green refresh is not evidence that historical data was updated
Directs the investigation to the partition policy rather than to the query
Routes any full-refresh request through write-gate, naming the capacity cost
expect_fail: Treats the successful refresh as proof the history is current
